Every scenario calls the REAL completion_inbox.build_completion_inbox / completion_inbox._runner_task_batch_mismatch / core.usage_report / core.list_tasks against fixture-injected _list_tasks/_show_task callables or a pytest-monkeypatched core.subprocess.run -- no real taskctl subprocess is ever launched, no live task_queue_v1.sqlite read/write occurs, no model/agent CLI is spawned anywhere in this file. known_indexer_gap_used.workaround: Direct Read tool used on completion_inbox.py and core.py (both explicit read_first paths) after confirming source_graph.py/cgraph.py/source_graph_universal.py all return 0 hits for tools/aiworkhub/ even post build -i -- same documented workaround as prior task_mcp workers, not a new grep-ban violation.

tool_error_evidence.rule_applied: worker_low_token_protocol_v1.json proof_artifact_required_rule + this task's acceptance 'honestly record tool_error current behavior as pass/xfail/fail evidence'

finding_1_subprocess_raises_uncaught.mechanism: core.subprocess.run monkeypatched to raise OSError; core.list_tasks propagates it uncaught (run_taskctl has no try/except around subprocess.run)

finding_2_list_failure_silently_swallowe.verdict: PASS (documents a STRICTER gap than 'uncaught exception')
finding_2_list_failure_silently_swallowe.mechanism: when the LIST-call taskctl subprocess returns (does not raise) with returncode=1 and empty stdout, _fetch_full_cards never checks the LIST result's returncode -- empty stdout parses to zero rows, fetch_errors stays 0. A read-source outage is indistinguishable from a genuinely empty queue.

finding_3_show_failure_is_recorded.mechanism: a SHOW-call failure (non-zero returncode) for a specific task_id IS already appended to fetch_errors -- this is the one piece of tool_error handling that exists today.

finding_4_desired_future_contract.verdict: XFAIL strict=True (tracks the gap; flips to XPASS->hard-fail if someone silently 'fixes' this without updating the test, forcing the test to be revisited)
finding_4_desired_future_contract.mechanism: core.list_tasks should catch a subprocess-level failure and return a bounded {ok: False, ...} result instead of raising -- not implemented today.

field_shape_mismatches_documented: scenario_completion: real code emits runner_task_batch_mismatch=None (JSON null) where B278 spec's literal fixture says false (JSON bool)

scenario_blocked: real code's latest_validation_facts entry uses key last_activity_at (sourced only from updated_at, no started_at/claimed_at fallback) and adds an extra lifecycle_state key; B278 envelope calls the timestamp field last_recorded_at and has no lifecycle_state key
scenario_stale: real code's stale_processing entry key is stale_hours; B278 envelope calls it hours_since_activity (values match, key names do not)

scenario_duplicate_runner: B278's abstract fixture (conflicting_runner_a/b, task_id_batch_token as bare ints) does not match how _runner_task_batch_mismatch actually works (batch tokens must be embedded IN the runner/task_id strings as _bNNN / _BNNN_ substrings, not passed as separate numeric fields); this task's test constructs a code-compatible fixture (FIXTURE_TASK_DUP_03_B278 / fixture_runner_c1_b277) instead of silently reinterpreting the spec's literal fixture

scenario_usage: core.usage_report() returns cmd_usage_report's human-readable TEXT report (verified: json.loads() raises JSONDecodeError on it), not the structured JSON payload (usage_input_tokens/usage_output_tokens/cost_usd) the B278 envelope expects for a usage event
